# Topic 1 — Choosing {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Cross-validated error

```{r}
set.seed(1)
fold <- sample(rep(1:10, length.out = nrow(ncd)))
cv_rmse <- function(fit_fun) sqrt(mean(sapply(1:10, function(k) { f <- fit_fun(ncd[fold != k, ]); mean((ncd$sbp[fold == k] - predict(f, ncd[fold == k, ]))^2) })))
round(c(linear = cv_rmse(function(d) lm(sbp ~ age + bmi + salt + activity + sex + smoker, d)),
        hinge = cv_rmse(function(d) lm(sbp ~ age + pmax(age - 45, 0) + bmi + salt + activity + sex + smoker, d)),
        ns4 = cv_rmse(function(d) lm(sbp ~ ns(age, 4) + bmi + salt + activity + sex + smoker, d)),
        gam = cv_rmse(function(d) gam(sbp ~ s(age) + s(bmi) + s(activity) + salt + sex + smoker, data = d, method = "REML")),
        ns15 = cv_rmse(function(d) lm(sbp ~ ns(age, 15) + bmi + salt + activity + sex + smoker, d))), 2)
```

::: {.incremental}
- **10-fold cross-validation**: fit on 9/10 of the data, **predict the held-out tenth**
- Linear **11.33**, hinge **11.27**, spline **11.28**, GAM **11.22**: curved models are **slightly better**; the gains are small because the **noise is large**
- **ns with 15 df: 11.29**: **more flexibility did not help**; it fits noise
- Choose the **simplest curve that fits** and is easy to explain
:::

## Decision guide

| Situation | Suggested approach |
|---|---|
| Curvature unknown | **GAM** or **ns() with 3 to 5 df**, then plot |
| Diminishing returns | **log** transform |
| Known threshold or bend | **hinge** at a justified knot |
| Small sample | few df (3), or linear and say so |
| Report to non-statisticians | **prediction plot**; hinge slopes if simple |
| Effect depends on another variable | **interaction**, plus simple slopes and risks |

# Topic 2 — Checking and extrapolation {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Marginal (standardised) predictions

```{r}
g_ns <- glm(cvd10 ~ age + ns(bmi, 4) + sex * smoker, data = ncd, family = binomial)
bmis <- c(18.5, 22, 25, 30, 35)
round(setNames(100 * sapply(bmis, function(b) mean(predict(g_ns, transform(ncd, bmi = b), type = "response"))), bmis), 1)
```

::: {.key}
The **average predicted risk if every adult had that BMI**: **13.8%** at 18.5, **6.1%** at 22, **4.7%** at 25, **11.8%** at 30, **39.6%** at 35. It averages over the **real mix** of age, sex and smoking, so it needs **no "typical person"**.
:::

## Do not extrapolate

```{r}
range(ncd$bmi); sum(ncd$bmi > 40)
```

::: {.warn}
BMI ranges from **14.5 to 40.1**, and **one adult** has a BMI above 40. A prediction at BMI 50 is **pure extrapolation** (the natural spline just continues in a straight line). Restrict plots and statements to the **range of the data**, and show where the data are thin (a **rug** or histogram).
:::

# Topic 3 — Reporting {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Reporting a non-linear effect

::: {.good}
- **A prediction plot** with a **95% band** (and a rug of the data)
- A **few contrasts** at meaningful values (e.g. OR for BMI 30 vs 24.6)
- The **test of non-linearity** (LR or F test)
- The **method**: spline type, **df** (and how chosen), knots
- **Never** a table of spline coefficients
:::

```{r}
ref <- predict(g_ns, transform(ncd[1, ], bmi = 24.6))
round(setNames(sapply(bmis, function(b) exp(predict(g_ns, transform(ncd[1, ], bmi = b)) - ref)), bmis), 1)
```

::: {.key}
OR compared with a BMI of 24.6: **3.8** (18.5), **1.4** (22), **1.0** (25), **3.1** (30), **21.5** (35): the **shape** is the message, not one odds ratio per unit.
:::

## An example sentence

::: {.key}
*"The 10-year risk of a cardiovascular event was U-shaped in BMI (natural spline, 4 df; likelihood-ratio test of non-linearity p < 0.001), lowest between BMI 24 and 25 and rising to 4.7% at BMI 25, 11.8% at 30 and 39.6% at 35 (standardised to the sample)."*
:::

## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("k5q1", "Cross-validated RMSE is 11.33 (linear), 11.27 (hinge), 11.28 (spline) and 11.22 (GAM). What is the most sensible conclusion?",
         c("The GAM is best, since it has the lowest RMSE of the four models compared here",
           "The linear model is best, since it has the fewest parameters of all the models",
           "The data are unusable, since all the differences are smaller than 0.1 mmHg",
           "Curvature helps a little: prefer a simple curve unless the GAM clearly wins"), answer = 4,
         explain = "The gain from curvature is real but small. A simple, explainable curve is preferred unless a more complex model is clearly better.")
```

## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("k5q2", "Why is a natural spline for age with 15 df a poor choice?",
         c("It follows the noise in the sample and predicts new data no better",
           "It cannot be fitted when there are fewer than 15 distinct ages",
           "It makes the model non-linear in the coefficients, so least squares fails",
           "It removes the age effect by splitting it across many terms"), answer = 1,
         explain = "Too much flexibility fits random variation, which does not repeat in new data. The cross-validated error is no better than with 4 df.")
```

## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("k5q3", "What is a marginal (standardised) predicted risk at BMI 30?",
         c("The predicted risk of the adult who has the median BMI of the sample",
           "The observed risk among the adults who happen to have a BMI of around 30",
           "The average predicted risk if every adult in the sample had a BMI of 30",
           "The predicted risk when every other variable in the model is set to zero"), answer = 3,
         explain = "Set BMI to 30 for everybody, predict for each adult with their own age, sex and smoking, and average. No single typical person is needed.")
```

## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("k5q4", "Why is it unwise to predict the risk at BMI 50 when only one adult has a BMI above 40?",
         c("The standard errors are zero outside the range of the data in the survey",
           "There are almost no data there, so the curve is just an extrapolation",
           "The spline cannot be evaluated outside the range of the knots it uses",
           "Predictions are limited to BMI values in the lowest quartile of the data"), answer = 2,
         explain = "Beyond the data the fitted curve is determined by the form of the spline, not by observations. Stay within the observed range and show where data are thin.")
```

## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("k5q5", "What is the best way to report a non-linear effect?",
         c("The p-value of each one of the spline coefficients, listed in a table",
           "A single odds ratio per unit of BMI taken from the straight-line model",
           "A prediction plot with a CI band, and a few contrasts at set values",
           "The degrees of freedom of the spline, together with its AIC value in a table"), answer = 3,
         explain = "Spline coefficients cannot be read one by one and a single OR hides the shape. A plot, a few contrasts and the test of non-linearity convey the result.")
```

## Score and take-home

**Your score: <span class="quiz-score"></span>**

::: {.incremental}
- **Cross-validate** and prefer the **simplest** adequate curve
- More df = **overfitting**
- **Standardised predictions** need no typical person
- **Do not extrapolate**; show where the data are
- Report **plot + contrasts + non-linearity test + df**
:::
